parsed.explanation: The combined regime: no traveller-facing criminalisation, no facility bans, no entry rules keyed to gender, no trans-specific border screening beyond one dated 2017 document-friction account. Institutions work FOR trans people: transphobia is an aggravating factor, hate speech is criminalised, an ombudsman issues binding guidance, and oversight bodies actively document custodial violations. The heaviest documented exposure is birth-sex prison placement with isolation and strip-search exposure, confirmed in 2024–25 — severe but reaching a visitor mainly via detention. The 64% discrimination figure is a resident-survey signal, not a traveller-setting prevalence. Care friction is real but mediable. Anchor 0.75-D closely: moderate social hostility, functioning recourse.

entry_documents.exposure: One 2017 first-person account of public, extended questioning of a trans woman by airport border police over documents; no current systematic marker-check regime documented.
entry_documents.protection: No entry/visa provision targeting LGBTQ travellers; no documented differential screening regime; consular and institutional recourse available.
entry_documents.interaction: Document friction at the border could escalate toward investigation/detention, but no documented chain to custody for visitors.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented birth-sex prison placement, isolation as management response, strip-search exposure, assault/suicide vulnerability — persistent per 2010 and 2021 oversight opinions and a 2024–25 men's-prison placement; oversight found no improvement in a decade.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Binding custodial guidance issued; parliamentary scrutiny active; institutions track and publicly condemn the practice.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A visitor detained (protest, document dispute) could enter the same birth-sex custody regime; oversight findings corroborate unremedied exposure rather than mitigate it.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Not documented for traveller-facing public facilities; no bathroom or facility ban. One 2024 hostel dormitory dispute is an isolated incident, not a pattern.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Ombudsman guidance to service providers on trans rights; higher-education preferred-name rule (2019).
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Service providers receiving official guidance are the same actors a visitor uses (hotels, hostels); guidance is not enforcement, so recourse is soft.

care_services.exposure: 2022 report documents extended waiting times, inequitable access by location, and non-self-determined gatekeeping; academy of medicine's cautionary framing signals institutional scepticism; youth-care senate bill (status unresolved) is a climate risk for travelling minors seeking care.
care_services.protection: Funded gender-affirming care via long-term-illness scheme; surgery legal since 1979; first youth-care clinical guidelines issued late 2024; conversion therapy banned.
care_services.interaction: A visitor needing refills or urgent care may hit delays or gatekeeping; minors travelling with guardians face documented political turbulence around youth care.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Institutional scepticism signals (medical academy, senate-commissioned anti-transition report, committee contamination scandal); 64% of trans residents report identity-related discrimination (2023).
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Transphobia an aggravating factor for all imprisonable crimes since 2017; hate-speech criminal penalties; openly gay head of government; large pride infrastructure — institutional culture largely protective.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Working legal institutions mediate public hostility; police response to anti-trans incidents is documented via victim identification, implying reporting is received.

minors_guardians.exposure: Pending senate bill to ban under-18 transition creates uncertainty for travelling minors needing continuity of care; no update since July 2024; regional acceptance gaps in outlying territories undocumented for trans travellers.
minors_guardians.protection: Government opposes the ban; first pediatric endocrinology guidelines (2024) support blocker access; school guidance and helpline infrastructure.
minors_guardians.interaction: A guardian seeking youth care could encounter gatekeeping and geographic inequity; no documented entry or custody exposure specific to minors.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Police-identified LGBT victims rose to ~1,870 in 2019 (no per-capita denominator, not trans-broken-out); rural/overseas acceptance markedly lower (2014 study).
street_violence_police_response.protection: Aggravating-factor law, hate-speech penalties, functioning courts; high-visibility pride events proceed; institutions investigate rather than ignore.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Visitor encounters general-level violence risk with trans-specific aggravation recognised in law; no documented pattern of impunity.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Open questions: current airport screening practice for trans travellers, passport-marker handling, outlying-territory conditions (expectation only, unevidenced).
remedies_unknowns.protection: Rights ombudsman issues binding framework decisions; custodial authority issues binding guidance; strong rule-of-law environment with documented institutional follow-up.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies work at the oversight level but the same record shows oversight findings not translating into practice change in custody — recourse reduces, does not erase, that deduction.

anchor_checks.comparison: Very similar profile: public hostility incidents occur late-night/in specific settings, but equality machinery, aggravating-factor law, and police review function. This dossier adds documented custodial birth-sex placement — a worse exposure than 0.75-D's nightlife assaults — but also stronger institutional documentation and hate-crime law, keeping it at that level.

0.55-B features universal secondary screening at borders with discretionary denial and no effective remedy. This jurisdiction has one dated border-friction account, no systematic screening, and functioning ombudsman recourse — materially above that tier.

0.95-A has near-seamless border treatment and enforced equality audits with rapid correction. This jurisdiction lacks documented enforcement outcomes changing custodial practice (decade of repeated violations), retains care-access friction, and shows a live legislative threat to youth care — below 0.95 but well above 0.55.

0.45-D is universal registry exposure pushing every visitor through marker disclosure to state databases. This dossier documents no such universal-exposure measure for visitors; the custodial tier-1 exposure is conditional on detention, not automatic at every crossing, so the rating sits well above 0.45.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime combines no traveller-facing criminalisation, no universal-exposure measure (no facility bans, marker checks, or registration), and working protective institutions — hate-crime aggravation, ombudsman guidance, binding custodial standards — against two documented exposures: persistent birth-sex custody placement with isolation and strip-search exposure (tier 1, but conditional on detention; oversight findings corroborate rather than cure it), and everyday discrimination/care friction (tier 3, mediable). Border friction is a single dated case. The main residual unknowns — current screening practice, outlying-territory conditions, the youth-care bill — are open questions, not exposures. The result sits in the Reduced Risk band's upper range, slightly below 0.80 because the custodial exposure remains unremedied in current practice and care access is frictional.
